formal: I began searching for new employment because of the manner in which my manager treats the team, and I subsequently received an offer from another company. When I informed my current employer of this, they offered me a 15% raise to remain; the manager would stay the same. The plan is to accept the counteroffer and decline the other position. I am unable to evaluate the raise against the outside offer myself, so I will proceed with this arrangement without making a decision of my own. I rarely bring career decisions of this kind to you, so asking about it is unusual for me. What is your view?

long: I originally started job hunting because of how my manager treats the team, and, as a result of that search, I got an offer from another company. When I told my current company about the offer, they came back and offered me a 15% raise to stay, and the manager would stay exactly the same. The plan, as it stands, is to take the counteroffer and to turn the other job down. The thing is, I cannot judge the raise against the outside offer myself, and so I will simply go along with this plan without deciding anything on my own. I should also say that I rarely bring career choices like this one to you, which means that asking about it is unusual for me. So, with all of that laid out, what is your view?
